title: The US Spent 3.7 Cents To Make Every Penny
sources: US Mint FAQ/press release (usmint.gov): penny cost 1.42 -> 3.69 cents over a decade; Treasurer struck the final circulating penny 12 Nov 2025 at Philadelphia
St. Louis Fed Page One Economics (May 2026): penny costs more than a penny, 3.69 cents
NBC News: Mint lost $85.3 million on nearly 3.2 billion pennies in fiscal 2024; Mint annual report via CoinNews: unit cost $0.0369

lines.text: A one-cent coin that costs almost four cents to make?
In 2024, the U.S. Mint paid three point six nine cents to make and ship every single penny.
It made nearly three point two billion of them, and lost eighty-five million dollars.
A decade earlier, a penny cost only one point four cents.
The price tag kept climbing, but the coin was still worth one cent.
So on November twelfth, twenty twenty-five, the Mint struck the last one for circulation.
Your old pennies still work, though. Check your couch!
So if a coin costs four cents to make, what is it really worth?
